items.title: How fast does a permissive signature's misuse-surface grow?
items.description: Models the two shapes compared throughout this unit: a permissive API (like Alertly's original SendAlertOptions, with several independent optional/boolean fields) versus a safe, discriminated-union API (like the redesigned AlertChannel). Each added optional/boolean field roughly doubles the number of combinations a caller could pass — most of them never intended or tested — while the safe design's number of valid states stays fixed at however many real channel kinds actually exist, regardless of how many fields those channels carry internally. Defaults (4 flags, 3 channels) match Alertly's own shape: emailAddress/phoneNumber/deviceToken/isUrgent as roughly-independent optional fields, against exactly 3 valid channel kinds in the redesign.

params.name: numberOfFlags
params.label: Optional/boolean fields on the permissive API

params.name: numberOfValidChannels
params.label: Valid states in the safe (union) design

items.compute: const n = params.numberOfFlags; const c = params.numberOfValidChannels; return { permissiveCombinations: Math.pow(2, n), safeCombinations: c };
